clinical_knowledge.topic: Acute Bacterial Rhinosinusitis evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Acute Bacterial Rhinosinusitis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management follows an evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for acute bacterial rhinosinusitis (ABRS) once diagnostic criteria are met (>10 days of symptoms or double-sickening), adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: facial pressure, nasal congestion, and yellow-green nasal discharge for 12 days

Key HPI features: 41F presents with 12 days of nasal congestion, facial pain and pressure over her cheeks, and thick yellow-green nasal discharge. Had a cold that improved on day 5 but then recurred with worse pain ('double sickening').

Objective/Exam findings: Tenderness to palpation over the bilateral maxillary sinuses; thick yellow-green purulent discharge in the nasal cavity; no facial swelling, periorbital edema, or vision changes.
Current medications: Fluticasone nasal spray daily
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Acute Bacterial Rhinosinusitis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Viral rhinosinusitis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Facial swelling or vision changes.
management_principles: Confirm ABRS criteria are met (symptoms >10 days without improvement, or double-sickening) before prescribing antibiotics
Prescribe Amoxicillin-Clavulanate (Augmentin) 875/125mg BID for 5-7 days if no penicillin allergy
Recommend nasal saline irrigation and intranasal steroid spray
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: A viral sinus infection superinfected by bacteria, marked by symptoms over 10 days or double-sickening, causing facial pressure and purulent discharge.

must_ask.say: How many days has this lasted, and did it improve then worsen?

history.answer: I've been dealing with a terrible stuffy nose, thick yellowish-green drainage, and intense pressure in my cheeks for almost two weeks now.
It started about 12 days ago with what felt like a typical head cold.
Around day 5 I actually felt like I was getting better, but then two days later it came back much worse with severe cheek pain and thicker mucus.
It's thick and yellowish-green, coming out of both nostrils all day long. It doesn't smell foul, though.
Both sides of my nose feel completely blocked up, and it's hard to breathe through my nose at all.
No, I haven't noticed any blood in the discharge or nosebleeds, and my face does not feel numb.
No, I haven't had sudden sneezing fits or itchy, watery eyes like I usually get with my seasonal allergies.
It has been pretty constant day and night since it came back, not really triggered by cold air, dust, or pets.
I have this heavy, throbbing ache right over both cheeks, and whenever I bend forward to pick something up, the pressure gets significantly worse.
No, my upper teeth don't feel sore or tender when I chew.
Yes, my sense of smell has been noticeably dull since my nose became so congested.
I felt warm and feverish for the last couple of days, though when I checked at home it was around 37.5 degrees.
No, my eyes don't feel swollen, and my vision has been completely normal with no blurriness or double vision.
I have a dull ache across my face, but no agonizing headache or stiffness in my neck.
Because my nose is so clogged, I've had to breathe through my mouth while sleeping, but my husband says I don't stop breathing or gasp at night.
Yes, I feel thick mucus constantly dripping down the back of my throat, which makes me clear my throat and cough a bit. No wheezing though.
No, I haven't used any over-the-counter decongestant sprays like oxymetazoline.
I don't have asthma, and taking aspirin or ibuprofen has never caused me to wheeze or feel short of breath.
No, I've never had any injury to my nose, no nasal surgeries, and no clear watery fluid leaking out.
No, I haven't had any dental work done recently, and I don't have any toothaches.
I think this started as a simple virus that has now turned into a bacterial sinus infection, so I probably need an antibiotic.
The intense cheek pain is really wearing me down and making it difficult to teach and get through the day.
I'm really hoping to get an antibiotic prescription today so this infection clears up quickly.
I have a history of allergic rhinitis, but no other chronic illnesses like high blood pressure or diabetes.
I've never had any surgeries and I have never been admitted to a hospital.
I use fluticasone nasal spray one spray in each nostril daily for my allergies, and I took some acetaminophen for the pain over the last two days.
No, I don't have any known allergies to medications.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I only drink a glass of wine on occasional weekends, maybe once or twice a month.
I work as an elementary school teacher, and I live at home with my husband and my daughter.
My mother has seasonal allergies, but there is no family history of asthma, polyps, or other serious medical problems.
My last menstrual period was two weeks ago, my cycles are regular every 28 days, and there is no chance I could be pregnant.

exam.finding: Alert, mildly uncomfortable woman with nasal voice, in no acute distress; no facial asymmetry or swelling.
Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, heart rate 74 bpm, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 37.4°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Marked tenderness on palpation over bilateral maxillary sinuses; frontal sinuses are non-tender.

Erythematous and swollen nasal mucosa with thick yellow-green purulent discharge in both middle meatuses; posterior pharynx shows mild cobblestoning and purulent postnasal drainage without tonsillar enlargement.
No periorbital edema, erythema, or proptosis; pupils are equal and reactive; extraocular movements are full and painless without diplopia.
Bilateral tympanic membranes are intact and pearly gray with normal light reflex, with no fluid or erythema.
No palpable cervical or submandibular lymphadenopathy, and no neck tenderness.
Neck is supple with full range of motion; negative Kernig and Brudzinski signs.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally without wheezing, crackles, or rhonchi.
